body:
### Summary

## Summary

Currently `uv auth` supports only static credentials. Modern infrastructure frequently supports authentication routines to be handled using the time-scoped tokens. This also is specifically useful if later the `Bearer` auth scheme will be implemented. Dynamic credentials can be injected with `keyring`, but this hardly can be called reliable.

This feature request proposes an approach to introduce the support for external token vending app different from `keyring`. The motivation, analysis and example of the implementation spec are provided below.

## Detailed Proposal

The pluggable credential providers is not new and there are similar issues and requests already touching the scope. See e.g. (#19025, #7660), but this requests attempts to address some concerns on security side mentioned in the discussions. There are also existing workarounds that allow to enable this "sideways".

The further proposal text is structured as follows: I start with the use cases, then proposal and finally with the alternatives review. But there's no design decision yet that either promise the implementation or block it.

### Use cases

In enterprise environments and specifically with cloud services the access might be managed with a short-lived tokens. Users usually posess the tool/script/routine that obtains or refreshes required tokens. In majority of cases tokens are passed in `Bearer` scheme by adding it to HTTP headers. But if the identity provider is in place it's usually not difficult to tweak the ingress to validate the tokens in the HTTP basic schema.

### Proposal Specification

Add the following functionality with no strong opinion on exact naming of the flags/options

- `uv auth login --token-provider "{command}" {service}` allows to store the `{command}` decomposed into the call + arguments array.
- During the authentication loop `uv` performs a call for the provided command and streams the output as HTTP basic with `__token__` username by default.
- **Optional implementation details**. 
    - `--username` is still allowed and overrides `__token__`.
    - Feature flag to turn on/off the functionality (if needed, alike `native-auth`)
- **Caching**. AFAIK current `uv` authentication workflow doesn't support probes for staleness, so if the token is cached and expired - auth will fail. The exact approach to caching might be a design discussion, baseline - no caching or few seconds caching, or more advanced with configurable lifetime. I have no strong preference, but believe it's not a blocker.
- **Security**. The vending call is done with user impersonation and execute arbitrary code without sandbox. So few points:
    - **Prohibited as part of code**. No way to specify the `token-vending` as part of any configuration provided with code. The approach does not support anything but explicit local setup using `uv auth` call. Providing such settings as part of `pyproject.toml/uv.toml` should be prohibited by design decision.
    - **Truncate output**. Output of the vending command is truncated by some (maybe configurable) max length.
    - **Prevent leaks to logs**. Vending call response is not logged.
    - **Protect config store**. If the vending call is stored as plain text in the credentials store - there's a risk that a third-party code will mutate the settings after `uv auth` calls. So storing in native store might be a better option, but require JSON support.
    - **No dynamic context**. Vending command is bound to service URL suffix, but user is responsible to path fixed service context as part of vending call definition if needed.
    - **Not a string**. Stored as command + arg list.

 ### Existing alternatives

1. **Wrappers/shims**. In this approach the actual `uv` command call is wrapped by adding a manual `UV_INDEX_{NAME}_PASSWORD` setup. E.g.

    ```sh
    UV_INDEX_EXAMPLE_PASSWORD=$(token-vending-cli -t service_name ...) path/to/uv
    ```    

    To wrap users either use `alias` approach or create a shell script that calls `uv`. This approach suffers from few problems for scaling it:

    - Using identically named script like `uv` that calls `uv` is not considered a good practice. It requires `PATH` modification and also binds the exact path to `uv` (to avoid cycles).
    - Using differently named scripts breaks agentic coding experience as they are well trained to use `uv`.
    - Using aliases doesn't work in non-interactive sessions.
    - Suffers in enterprises as exact approach is OS-dependent.

2.  **Keyring**. There's a path to actually quickly generate a trivial `keyring` backend that will do the wrapping of the call to a token vendor. This is a closest alternative. But let's look at configuration efforts. E.g. I am fine with having `keyring` as a `uv tool`.

    ```sh
    # install keyring with custom backend
    uv tool install keyring --with {my_backend_path}

    # further configuration of keyring might be needed (priority of backends)
    ```

    This is what outlines the experience with this approach:
    - `keyring` is famous to have unstable behavior in Linux. Since keyring initializes all backends on every call - it may fail on system keyring backend even if it's not used.
    - `{my_backend_path}` will either have to be a GIT direct link or a PyPI.org package. The reason is that we are avoiding the chicken-egg problem, we cannot install packages from private indexes yet. Publishing to PyPI.org is not always preferrable, having GIT link technically works, but requires the user to set up authentication for non-public GIT index.
    - Mess with priorities. Some users might use `keyring` somewhere else, so changing priorities globally is unwanted as they might want to have priority of system keyring higher. That will ensure that we lose time on the call to system keyring, and in case of stale old credentials stored in the system keyring chaining to our custom backend won't happen.

    With all the difficulties, this is still a closest option to enable scalable configuration for enterprises.

## Final notes

The design spec is a **proposal**, not requirement. The proposal is based on the assumed architectural design decision that we aim to simplify and unify auth management on `uv` side, without necessity to use third-party packages. **Clarification of the direction is really appreciated**.

The proposal duplicates (correlates) with (#19025, #7660), but slightly differently defines the mechanism. Also no decision is taken in the mentioned items.

The implementation likely should wait for the #18907 to complete, as it might rely on the features that are already seen in Draft.

I'm eager to attempt contributing this if the proposal is supported.

### Example

Example is OS specific, I use MacOS. The `get_token_cli` is a custom application assumed to be available in the user machine. This is also an ideal one that assumes no feature flags required.

```sh
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# bearer (if ever) or basic with `__token__` username.
uv auth login --token-provider "get_token_cli -t pypi.company.com ..." pypi.company.com
```

For the cases the HTTP authentication requires non `__token__` username
```sh
# basic with custom_username
uv auth login \
  --token-provider "get_token_cli -t pypi.company.com ..." \
  --username custom_username \
  pypi.company.com
```

Now taken that configuration for the private index is provided in `uv.toml` or `pyproject.toml` (context dependent) user is ready authenticate.
title: Feature request: `uv auth` supports pluggable token provider for short-lived tokens
